title: HDiv-VIM (HACApK charge-Gram) vs collocation MMMM: matrix-BUILD scalability
measured_on: mdx (quiet compute host -- timing MUST be on mdx per CLAUDE.md Benchmark Policy)
element_note: PRELIMINARY on TET: released radia 4.95.5 HDiv-VIM is TET-only; the AUTHORITATIVE hex-vs-hex build-scaling (the paper's element) is PENDING the pure-hex HDiv-VIM reaching mdx (release or push_pyds_to_mdx after the codex hex WIP settles). The HACApK build-scalability finding (compression -> near-linear build) is element-type-general (an H-matrix property), so the tet trend is expected to carry to hex.
problem: unit cube, linear soft iron mu_r=1000, uniform H0=200 kA/m, HACApK eps=1e-4
mmmm_build_metric: GetSolveStats t_moment_system_build + t_hmatrix_build (isolated); EMPTY {} at large N (radia stats not recorded on the large-N method-2 path -> mmmm_build=null there)
hdiv_build_exponent_note: log-log fit hdiv_build_s ~ n_charge^1.23 over n_charge 602..21423 -- NEAR-LINEAR, i.e. the HACApK charge-Gram makes the build SCALABLE (a dense face-face Coulomb Gram would be ~N^2).
crossover: HDiv build reaches PARITY with MMMM build at ~34k HDiv DoF (~10k charges, ntet~5346); below that MMMM build is up to ~5x faster (H-matrix overhead + weak compression at small N).
conclusion: HDiv-VIM's only weakness (the heavy singular-Gram matrix build) is neutralized by the HACApK charge-Gram at engineering scale: the build scales ~N^1.2 and becomes comparable to the moment method's build by ~34k DoF. This supports a TIERED role split (HDiv for large-scale/accurate/loop-free, MMMM for the fast small-N/coarse tier), NOT one method replacing the other.
